title: Choir and Oath
premise: Casper Brightwater, the last swordspeaker whose oaths can reshape reality, has hidden their magic for a decade in the anti-magical city of Vellum's Reach. When a date named Wren Halloway turns up in a century-old prophecy book as the soul promised to the court beneath the mountain, Casper realizes their own name is on the next page. To save Wren and themselves, Casper must reclaim the oath they swore away years ago, descend into the goblin court to steal back two souls, and finally choose whether inheritance is a chain or a gift. The story ends with Casper breaking the prophecy itself—rewriting the oath so that no one is ever bound again—and choosing to stay in Vellum's Reach, visible at last.
about_author: Rafael Zhou is the pen name of a former choir singer turned fantasy writer who grew up between two languages and never quite belonged to either. They write stories about people who inherit things they never asked for, and live in a drafty apartment full of half-finished sheet music.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the market of Vellum's Reach, Casper sells harmless luck-charms while hiding the oath-scar on their palm, then meets Wren Halloway, a cartographer with ink-stained fingers and an unsettling familiarity. The beat is quiet longing: Casper wants connection but has practiced invisibility for ten years, and Wren sees through it immediately.

chapters.title: The Book That Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following Wren to the archive where she works, Casper finds a prophecy book written a century ago depicting their date in exacting detail—and their own name beneath hers, listed as 'the Brightwater debt.' The emotional beat is dread: the past Casper fled has been waiting patiently, and it knows their address.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Swore
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a flashback chapter of grandmother Maren teaching young Casper the first oath. Casper learns Maren sold her own soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy the family's safety—a debt that passed down like eye color. The beat is grief tangled with anger: love and betrayal wearing the same face.

chapters.title: The Oathbreakers' Guild
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, revealed as a descendant of the guild that once hunted swordspeakers, offers Casper her help and her guild's forbidden records. Their fragile trust cracks when Casper learns what her ancestors did. The beat is wounded honesty: both carry inherited guilt neither chose, and saying it aloud is the first real intimacy either has known.

chapters.title: Nine Bells for the Debt
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The city's Bell Wardens, enforcers of the magic ban, raid Casper's shop after an anonymous tip. Casper must use a small oath publicly to escape—shattering ten years of cover. The beat is terror turning exhilirating: being seen is dangerous, but hiding is starting to feel like dying slowly.

chapters.title: The Road Under
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper and Wren flee into the old mining roads toward the mountain court, pursued by Wardens and shadowed by a goblin herald named Sess who claims Casper's grandmother still lives—as collateral. The beat is reluctant partnership hardening into devotion on the road, with Sess as an unnervingly courteous guide.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the goblin court, Casper finds Maren diminished but unbroken, and learns the truth: she didn't sell her soul—she traded it to imprison something older that the court keeps fed on borrowed souls. Wren's name is next on the ledger. The beat is vertigo: every certainty about family history collapses.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While Casper confronts Maren, Wren infiltrates the court's archive to strike her own name from the ledger, discovering the imprisoned thing—the First Speaker—is waking because the oaths that bind it are fraying with each generation. The beat is desperate agency: Wren refuses to be a page in anyone's book.

chapters.title: Swordsong
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The climax: the First Speaker breaks free, offering Casper unlimited power if they renew the ancient binding with their own soul. Instead, Casper speaks a new kind of oath—not a binding but a release—unmaking the prophecy, freeing Maren, the court's stolen souls, and themselves, at the cost of their swordspeaker gift burning out forever. The beat is sacrifice transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: Choir and Oath
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Above ground again, Casper powerless but free, opens a small school where children learn words without fear, with Wren mapping the roads below so none are lost there again. Maren, aging humanly now, visits often. The final beat is belonging: Casper signs their full name—Brightwater and all—on the school's door, visible at last, and it feels like coming home.
